newsitem.title: FRANCE: Controllers' strike disrupts French trains.
newsitem.headline: Controllers' strike disrupts French trains.

text.p: A fresh strike by train controllers began affecting French rail traffic on Wednesday and the state-run railway company SNCF said disruption was likely to worsen later in the day and extend to Friday afternoon.
The strike started biting even before it officially began at 8 p.m. (1800 GMT).

High-speed trains to Belgium and Eurostar trains to London through the Channel tunnel were unaffected, but traffic was cut by one third on the Paris-Lyon-Marseille high-speed route and various regional routes.

Controllers, who are also responsible for train security and staged a disruptive 48-hour stoppage last month, are protesting against planned job cuts on regional routes and demanding negotiations on bonuses.

SNCF management said in a statement it was willing to pursue talks on union demands opened several weeks ago but it could not improve its offers because of financial constraints and the need to preserve fairness among the company's staff.
